newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ENERGY COMPANY MULLS EUROBOND ISSUE-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ENERGY COMPANY MULLS EUROBOND ISSUE-REPORT.

text.p: Lithuanian Energy is mulling the idea of launching a eurobond next year to boost its working capital, the newspaper Lietuvos rytas reported on Thursday.
The newspaper quoted Rimvydas Rukshenas, the director general of the firm, as saying that they have not decided on how big the issue might be and that it would be used to buy fuel.
The company may also hold a tender for a financial advisor and apply for a credit rating, the newspaper said.

Lithuanian Energy is a state-run firm which has shed its unprofitable domestic heating section and passed it to the control of local governments. It has preserved its profitable electric production sector.
